swett-legitimacy.speaker: Laura Swett, FERC Chairman
swett-legitimacy.evidence: PJM is facing a grave legitimacy crisis. Some transmission owners are openly discussing leaving the RTO altogether. Put plainly, market participants have lost confidence in PJM's decision-making abilities.

lacerte-quagmire.speaker: David LaCerte, FERC Commissioner
lacerte-quagmire.evidence: This is a cultural quagmire that they've developed by eroding the board in the past and creating this fear of [board members] being terminated to where they're not using their authorities. They're not engaging with the states because they don't want to get out of line with what the stakeholders want.

mills-committed.speaker: David Mills, PJM President and CEO
mills-committed.evidence: We are fully committed to rise to the challenge.

ferc-september.speaker: Utility Dive report of the Commission's stated next steps
ferc-september.evidence: FERC will hold a dispute resolution forum in September with PJM stakeholders to develop a governance reform package. If no agreement is reached by end of September, FERC will impose its own reforms on PJM.

fr-conference-date.speaker: FERC, Notice of Commission-Led Technical Conference (Docket AD26-7-000)
fr-conference-date.evidence: The technical conference will convene on Thursday, July 23, 2026, in the Kevin J. McIntyre Commission Meeting Room at the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission, 888 First Street NE, Washington, DC 20426. The conference will discuss PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.'s (PJM) governance and stakeholder process, with a particular focus on identifying and evaluating actionable reforms to improve PJM's ability to address system needs in a timely and efficient manner.

isone-abeyance.speaker: ISO New England (ISO Newswire)
isone-abeyance.evidence: ISO New England and the region's transmission owners intend to request a 90-day abeyance as part of compliance with a show cause order issued by the Federal Energy Regulatory Commission (FERC). The ISO and transmission owners must submit interconnection process modifications by November 16, 2026, following the abeyance period if approved. By July 20, the ISO must file with FERC an informational report on resource adequacy in the context of large loads.

isone-report.speaker: ISO New England (ISO Newswire)
isone-report.evidence: ISO-NE has made an informational filing on regional resource adequacy and has begun to outline potential rule changes, including requiring new large loads to bring incremental new generation, and not procuring capacity through the regional capacity market to serve these large loads. During a July 16 presentation to the NEPOOL Transmission Committee, ISO-NE outlined plans to request a 90-day abeyance of the show cause proceeding.

pjm-bra.speaker: PJM Interconnection news release
pjm-bra.evidence: PJM's 2028/2029 Base Residual Auction procured 138,318 MW of unforced capacity. The price came in at the FERC-approved cap of $325/MW-day (UCAP) for the entire PJM footprint. The cleared supply procured in the auction times the clearing price totals $16.4 billion. The capacity of the resources procured in the auction, plus FRR resources, is short of PJM's 20% installed reserve margin target by 6,831 MW. PJM continues to hold a reserve margin of 14.7% for the 2028/2029 Delivery Year.

lacerte-wires.speaker: David LaCerte, FERC Commissioner
lacerte-wires.evidence: status quo is really untenable. Looking at things differently is hard, especially in entrenched utilities that have been doing this for a long time. We have a lot of other models at other RTOs and ISOs across the country that are much more functional. We need to make sure that the incentives that we give are properly tailored to actually meet the goals.
lacerte-wires.note: Utility Dive renders the first phrase as a partial quote inside its own sentence ('The PJM Interconnection's "status quo is really untenable"'), so only the words inside the inner quotation marks are his; the site quotes that fragment and no more.

md-delegation-letter.speaker: Maryland Congressional Delegation (Sens. Van Hollen and Alsobrooks; Reps. Hoyer, Mfume, Raskin, Ivey, Elfreth, McClain Delaney and Olszewski)
md-delegation-letter.occasion: Letter to FERC Chairman Swett, July 27, 2026
md-delegation-letter.evidence: We were encouraged by the Commission's June 18, 2026 orders directing PJM and five other grid operators to justify or reform how they assign the costs of serving large loads, which advance the essential goal of protecting ordinary consumers. We urge the Commission to act expeditiously to provide relief from these costs for Maryland ratepayers, including as requested in OPC's complaint.
md-delegation-letter.note: Read directly from the signed PDF with fitz, not from a summary. The letter cites $22 billion in PJM projects advanced principally to serve data centers, roughly $2 billion of it assigned to Maryland ratepayers, and an estimated $1.6 billion on Maryland bills over ten years, $823 million of it residential, about $345 for the average customer. It asks for relief as requested in the Maryland OPC complaint at Docket EL26-63, not for retroactive refunds.

spanberger-scc.speaker: Abigail Spanberger, Governor of Virginia
spanberger-scc.occasion: Statement on the Virginia SCC order, August 10, 2026
spanberger-scc.evidence: I am proud that after my administration urged state regulators to protect Virginia families and small businesses from shouldering the cost of new transmission infrastructure meant to serve data centers, the SCC listened. This order \u2014 which is projected to save Virginians hundreds of millions of dollars \u2014 makes sure that data centers are paying the full cost of the transmission infrastructure their developments require.
spanberger-scc.note: The release does not mention FERC or PJM; it is state retail action running parallel to the federal proceeding.

sherrill-fairshare.speaker: Mikie Sherrill, Governor of New Jersey
sherrill-fairshare.occasion: Signing of the Data Center Fair Share Act (S731/A796), July 7, 2026
sherrill-fairshare.evidence: For too long, New Jersey families have paid the price for poor oversight, outdated policies, and rising demand on our electric grid by unchecked actors.
sherrill-fairshare.note: The bill creates a data-center ratepayer class, requires large loads to curtail before residential customers on a strained grid, and lets large loads offset capacity obligations by funding demand reduction elsewhere.

opsi-forcefully-oppose.speaker: Organization of PJM States and PJM Governors' Collaborative
opsi-forcefully-oppose.occasion: Letter to PJM Board Chair Paula Conboy, September 29, 2026, the day before the Members Committee vote
opsi-forcefully-oppose.evidence: Should the Members nonetheless approve their term sheet, the states will forcefully oppose it before the Commission and beyond.
opsi-forcefully-oppose.note: Read in full from the one-page PDF posted by PJM. Added by the 2026-10-08 sweep; the file-level captured_at predates it.

pjmmc1022-abeyance.speaker: PJM staff
pjmmc1022-abeyance.occasion: Special Members Committee consultation deck, posted Oct 15, 2026 for the Oct 22 meeting (slide 2)
pjmmc1022-abeyance.evidence: PJM submitted a motion for abeyance of the paper hearing on October 12 and notified FERC that it plans to submit a new 205 filing to FERC on October 29th to address these elements, and a few additional updates.

pjmmc1022-elements.speaker: PJM staff
pjmmc1022-elements.evidence: Key elements of upcoming 205 filing: Cost Allocation LSE Exit Responsibilities LSE Collateral Requirement

pjmmc1022-optout.speaker: PJM staff
pjmmc1022-optout.evidence: Remove the opt out for muni/co-ops. FERC noted that this opt out appeared to be unduly discriminatory because cooperatives and municipal utilities serve Large Loads that are similarly situated to Large Loads served by other Load Serving Entities.

pjmmc1022-timeline.speaker: PJM staff
pjmmc1022-timeline.occasion: Same deck, slide 16 (2027 Proposed RBP Timeline)
pjmmc1022-timeline.evidence: Open RBP March 1 Closes March 22 RBP Results Posted May 3 Final Target/Supply Determined April 21

pjmto1009-commit.speaker: PJM Transmission Owners Agreement Administrative Committee
pjmto1009-commit.occasion: Notice of consultation with the Members Committee, Oct 9, 2026 (p. 1)
pjmto1009-commit.evidence: The PJM Transmission Owners have committed to submit their proposed revisions to address the concerns identified by the June 18, 2026 order issued in Docket No. EL26-67-000 via a Federal Power Act (“FPA”) Section 205 filing on or before November 16, 2026.

pjmto1009-scope.speaker: PJM Transmission Owners Agreement Administrative Committee
pjmto1009-scope.evidence: the proposed revisions to the Tariff may also include a cost allocation methodology associated with PJM’s proposed consolidated generation and transmission service process.

isone1009-205.speaker: ISO New England
isone1009-205.occasion: Large Loads Integration Proposal Information summary, last update Oct 9, 2026
isone1009-205.evidence: The ISO and the Participating Transmission Owners Administrative Committee (PTO AC) were granted an abeyance and will develop a Section 205 filing to be submitted by November 16, 2026.

shields-burdened.speaker: Jeffrey Shields, PJM spokesman
shields-burdened.evidence: honoring the concept that existing electricity customers should not be unfairly burdened by new, energy intensive customers

jefferies-ipps.speaker: Jefferies analysts
jefferies-ipps.occasion: Client note reported by Utility Dive, Oct 12, 2026
jefferies-ipps.evidence: the latest development is positive for existing generation/IPPs

miso-lars.speaker: MISO (filing, as quoted by Utility Dive)
miso-lars.evidence: LARS provides MISO with a targeted tool to address the intersection of significant large load additions,

pjm-reviewing-0930.speaker: PJM Interconnection (statement)
pjm-reviewing-0930.evidence: PJM is reviewing the order and intends to work quickly to address the Commission’s remaining concerns. We remain focused on advancing solutions that maintain reliability, appropriately allocate costs to the customers driving those costs, and protect consumers as the region navigates significant demand growth.

souder-unsustainable.speaker: David Souder, Executive Director, PJM System Operations
souder-unsustainable.occasion: PJM Planning Committee, Sept 8, 2026, as reported by Inside Lines Sept 10
souder-unsustainable.evidence: This type of operation is unsustainable and needs to be addressed,

pjmil0910-november.speaker: PJM Inside Lines
pjmil0910-november.evidence: PJM plans to file proposed solutions to FERC in November.

naruc0618-states.speaker: Ann Rendahl, NARUC President (Washington Utilities and Transportation Commission)
naruc0618-states.evidence: “We appreciate the Commissioners’ comments at today’s meeting recognizing the critical role of states and state regulators given the jurisdictional division of duties under the Federal Power Act. We also appreciate the Commissioners’ focus on reliability and affordability, noting the need for transparency in setting wholesale transmission rates, which has been a key issue raised by our members, as these costs are passed directly through to end-use customers. “The record in these proceedings has demonstrated much good work already taking place at the state level regarding large load interconnection. States remain committed to ensuring the appropriate allocation of costs across all customer classes and working constructively with our federal colleagues to that end.”

hklaw0623-jurisdiction.speaker: Holland & Knight (Gulstone, Forshay, Kalpin, Phillips, Coates, Connors, Martell)
hklaw0623-jurisdiction.evidence: Importantly, FERC did not assert any new or expanded jurisdiction over retail load or co-located load in a broad or preemptive sense. Instead, the Commission reaffirmed and carefully cabined its existing jurisdiction while explicitly leaving core retail-level questions to the states.

mdopc0717-assumes.speaker: David S. Lapp, Maryland People’s Counsel
mdopc0717-assumes.occasion: OPC release on its July 17, 2026 filing in EL26-67
mdopc0717-assumes.evidence: “FERC’s order will help expose data center cost shifts by making them more transparent to state regulators and consumers, but the Federal Power Act requires PJM to also fix its rules that allocate data center costs to other customers,” Lapp said. “The order erroneously assumes State regulators have authority that they do not clearly have.” ... OPC’s filing was joined by the Office of the Ohio Consumers’ Counsel, the Delaware Division of the Public Advocate, and the Office of the Illinois Attorney General.

udadvocates0721-joint.speaker: Ratepayer advocates from Delaware, Illinois, Maryland and Ohio (joint filing, as quoted by Utility Dive)
udadvocates0721-joint.evidence: Ratepayer advocates from Delaware, Illinois, Maryland and Ohio asked FERC to respond as quickly as possible. “Each network upgrade added to a transmission owner’s revenue requirement while these questions remain open embeds another cost shift, and every cost-recovery agreement negotiated against an unsettled standard invites the disputes the Commission could resolve today,” they said.

udadvocates0721-paoca.speaker: Pennsylvania Office of Consumer Advocate (separate filing, as quoted by Utility Dive)
udadvocates0721-paoca.evidence: Even with cost-recovery agreements, PJM’s regional cost allocation rules may cause cost shifts, according to Pennsylvania’s ratepayer advocate. “Unjust and unreasonable wholesale transmission cost shifts from large loads in PJM can manifest through unjust and unreasonable cost allocation of both [Regional Transmission Expansion Plan] projects and supplemental projects, not just by speculative large loads failing to pay their existing share under existing cost allocation methods,” the Pennsylvania ratepayer advocate said.

peskoe0720-violates.speaker: Ari Peskoe, Harvard Law School Electricity Law Initiative
peskoe0720-violates.evidence: Advocates from 4 states (DE, IL, MD, OH) argue that FERC's June order merely punts consumer protection to states. That move violates the law. PJM's Tariff guarantees cost shifts due to transmission for data centers. Only FERC can fix that. And it must.

peskoe0723-spread.speaker: Ari Peskoe, Harvard Law School Electricity Law Initiative
peskoe0723-spread.evidence: But FERC didn't order any changes to how utilities share the costs of those upgrades with everyone. It did not order the utilities to charge those upgrade costs to data centers. They are still spread to everyone.

wypr0826-langree.speaker: Claire Lang-Ree, NRDC Sustainable FERC Project
wypr0826-langree.occasion: WYPR, August 26, 2026, on PJM's backstop proposal as filed
wypr0826-langree.evidence: "PJM is saying very clearly to the data centers, 'We will no longer buy power on your behalf,' and that's going to have a really good impact on prices in the long run, and make sure that the rest of us aren't basically subsidizing power for data centers," Lang-Ree said.

wypr0826-lapp.speaker: David Lapp, Maryland People’s Counsel
wypr0826-lapp.occasion: WYPR, August 26, 2026, on PJM's backstop proposal as filed
wypr0826-lapp.evidence: "If the data centers don't show up in those zones, then it'll be the existing customers, ordinary households included, that will pay those costs. So for Maryland customers, and it really applies to customers of Potomac Edison and Baltimore Gas and Electric, there are more than half a billion dollars in costs that could potentially fall to ordinary customers," Lapp said.

peskoe0930-surprising.speaker: Ari Peskoe, Harvard Law School Electricity Law Initiative
peskoe0930-surprising.evidence: Surprising! FERC has issues with the cost allocation framework that determined who pays for this data center capacity auction.

doe1009-wright.speaker: Chris Wright, U.S. Secretary of Energy
doe1009-wright.evidence: “The Trump Administration remains committed to doing everything it can to lower electricity costs, grow the supply of American energy and strengthen grid reliability,” said U.S. Secretary of Energy Chris Wright. “That’s why President Trump created the Ratepayer Protection Pledge, and the Energy Department supports having large electricity users pay for reliable new power generation.”

dennisx1012-states.speaker: Jeff Dennis
dennisx1012-states.evidence: I'm not sure what time the order came out, but late Friday @FERC delivered another blow to @pjminterconnect 's ongoing efforts to try to get a handle on large load growth and stabilize its markets. In doing so, it appears to be putting more pressure on states to find answers. 1/

latitude1013-yang.speaker: Mary Yang, former regulatory counsel for PJM and chief operating officer at 804 Advisory
latitude1013-yang.evidence: Now, Yang added, the uncertainty “is going to keep dragging,” in part because PJM is juggling a number of competing priorities, and re-writing IRAS rules isn’t likely to be the top one. “It does slow down the development of these more innovative bilateral mechanisms to solve some of these problems,” Yang added.

bisnow1014-langree.speaker: Claire Lang-Ree, NRDC Sustainable FERC Project
bisnow1014-langree.occasion: Emailed statement quoted by Bisnow, October 14, 2026
bisnow1014-langree.evidence: "At a minimum, PJM's rules must require data centers to bring their own supply, and not allow them to raise electricity costs or cause blackouts," Lang-Ree said in an emailed statement.

udduke1013-rosner.speaker: David Rosner, FERC Commissioner (concurring in the Oct 9 Duke Energy Carolinas order, as quoted by Utility Dive)
udduke1013-rosner.occasion: Utility Dive, October 13, 2026; the concurrence itself was not read
udduke1013-rosner.evidence: “Duke’s proposal offers meaningful, if imperfect, new protections, and for that reason the commission is right to accept it,” FERC Commissioner David Rosner said in a concurring statement ... “To the extent state regulatory actions are not sufficient to protect consumers, the commission has an obligation to seriously consider expanding the cost recovery framework it established in the Large Load Show Cause Orders,” Rosner said.

udduke1013-chang.speaker: Judy Chang, FERC Commissioner (separate statement in the Oct 9 Duke Energy Carolinas order, as quoted by Utility Dive)
udduke1013-chang.occasion: Utility Dive, October 13, 2026; the statement itself was not read
udduke1013-chang.evidence: “I do not believe [Duke Energy Carolinas] has demonstrated that its filing represents an acceptable level of customer protection, and the precedent the commission establishes here takes a step backwards from the strong arguments set forth in the Large Load Show Cause Orders,” Chang said.
